recipe.title: Thiof Yassa au four avec riz brisé
recipe.description: Filets de thiof marinés au citron et aux oignons, cuits au four jusqu’à une chair tendre, servis avec du riz brisé parfumé.
instructions: Émince les 2 oignons.
Coupe les 2 tomates en dés.
Dans un bol, mélange les filets de thiof (300 g) avec le jus de citron, 1 c. à soupe d'huile d'arachide, 1 pincée de sel, 1 pincée de poivre et la moitié du piment haché.
Dispose les filets marinés dans un plat allant au four.
Répartis les oignons émincés et les dés de tomates autour du poisson, ajoute le reste du piment.
Couvre le plat de papier aluminium et enfourne à 180 °C pendant 20 minutes (feu moyen), jusqu’à ce que le poisson atteigne 63 °C au centre et que la chair se détache facilement.
Pendant ce temps, rince le riz brisé (200 g) puis fais-le cuire dans 400 ml d’eau à feu moyen pendant 12 minutes, jusqu’à absorption complète, puis retire du feu.
Sors le poisson du four, retire le papier aluminium, laisse reposer 2 minutes, puis sers avec le riz chaud.
Saupoudre éventuellement d’un peu de piment frais pour la touche finale.
tips: Si tu n’as pas de citron, ajoute un peu de vinaigre blanc pour l’acidité.
Le papier aluminium empêche le poisson de se dessécher tout en permettant aux arômes de se concentrer.

recipe.title: Soupe épicée de manioc et chou
recipe.description: Une soupe réconfortante à base de manioc et de chou, relevée d’une pointe de tomate et de concentré, parfaite pour un dîner léger.
instructions: Épluche le manioc (400 g) et coupe‑le en cubes d’environ 2 cm.

Ajoute l’oignon émincé et fais‑le dorer 3 minutes, jusqu’à ce qu’il devienne translucide.
Incorpore les dés de tomate, le concentré de tomate et le piment haché, mélange 2 minutes.

Assaisonne avec 1 pincée de sel et 1 pincée de poivre, goûte et ajuste le piment si besoin.
Verse la soupe dans des bols et sers immédiatement.

Si tu préfères une texture plus onctueuse, mixe une partie de la soupe avant d’ajouter le chou.

recipe.title: Riz sauté aux restes de thiof et légumes
recipe.description: Riz brisé sauté avec des filets de thiof restants, oignon, tomate et une pointe de piment, un plat rapide et anti-gaspi.
instructions: Rince le riz brisé (300 g) puis mets‑le dans une casserole avec 600 ml d’eau, porte à ébullition, puis fais cuire à feu doux 12 minutes, jusqu’à absorption complète. Étale le riz sur un plat pour le refroidir rapidement.

Assaisonne avec 1 pincée de sel et 1 pincée de poivre, goûte et ajuste si besoin.

recipe.title: Hearty Beef and Spinach Stew with Peanut‑Enriched Plantain Dumplings
recipe.description: A comforting one‑pot stew that combines tender beef, nutrient‑rich spinach, and creamy ground peanuts, served with soft plantain dumplings. Perfect for a filling lunch and can be made ahead.
instructions: Dice the beef into 2‑cm cubes.
Peel the plantains, mash them with a fork, and set aside.
Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.
Toast the raw peanuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 4 minutes, stirring, until golden and fragrant; then grind them in a mortar or food processor to a coarse powder.
In a large pot, heat a splash of water over medium heat, add the beef cubes, and brown them for 5 minutes, turning until all sides are seared.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot; sauté for 3 minutes on medium heat, until the onion becomes translucent.
Stir in the ground peanuts and cook for another 2 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
Pour in 800 ml of water, increase to a gentle boil, then reduce to a low simmer. Cover and cook for 25 minutes, until the beef is tender.
While the stew simmers, shape the mashed plantain into small dumplings (about the size of a walnut) and gently drop them into the pot during the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Add the spinach, stirring until it wilts, about 2 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Check the beef temperature: it should reach at least 63 °C and be easy to pull apart.
Serve the stew hot, ensuring each bowl gets a few plantain dumplings and a generous spoonful of the peanut‑rich broth.
tips: If you prefer a thicker broth, blend half of the cooked peanuts with a little broth before adding back to the pot.
Leftovers taste even better after a night in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Baked Peanut‑Crusted Plantain & Spinach Salad
recipe.description: Crispy baked plantain slices coated in a savory peanut crust, tossed with fresh spinach, caramelized onions, and a light garlic‑peanut dressing. A satisfying cold‑or‑room‑temperature lunch.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Peel the plantains and slice them diagonally into ½‑cm thick rounds.
Place the plantain rounds on a baking sheet, drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil, and toss to coat.
Toast the raw peanuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring, then let cool and pulse them into coarse crumbs.
Spread the peanut crumbs on a shallow plate; press each oiled plantain round into the crumbs, coating both sides.
Bake the coated plantain rounds on the preheated oven for 20 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp.
While the plantains bake, thinly slice the onion into ribbons and mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
In a large salad bowl, combine the fresh spinach and onion ribbons; drizzle with the garlic‑lemon dressing and toss gently.
When the plantain rounds are done, let them cool for 2 minutes, then arrange them on top of the dressed spinach salad.
Serve immediately or store at room temperature for up to 4 hours.
tips: For extra crunch, add a handful of whole raw peanuts on top just before serving.
If you like a spicier note, sprinkle a pinch of chili powder onto the plantain before baking.

recipe.title: Spicy Beef, Peanut & Plantain Soup
recipe.description: A robust, aromatic soup featuring tender beef, sweet plantain chunks, and a velvety peanut broth, brightened with spinach and a hint of garlic. Ideal for a quick, warming lunch.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite‑size strips.
Peel the plantains and cut them into 1‑cm cubes.
Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.
Place the raw peanuts in a pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil over medium heat; simmer for 10 minutes, then drain and set aside.
In the same pot, add 900 ml fresh water and bring to a boil.
Add the beef strips, onion, and garlic to the boiling water; simmer on medium heat for 12 minutes, until the beef starts to turn opaque.
Stir in the cooked peanuts and use a immersion blender to blend the soup until the broth is smooth and creamy (about 2 minutes).
Add the plantain cubes and continue to simmer for 10 minutes, until the plantain is tender and the broth thickens.
Add the spinach leaves and cook for 2 minutes, just until wilted.
Season with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of chili flakes. Check beef temperature: it must reach at least 63 °C and be no longer pink.
Ladle the hot soup into bowls and serve immediately.
tips: For a richer flavor, toast the peanuts before boiling them.
Adjust the heat level by increasing or decreasing the chili flakes.

recipe.title: Guiso de lentejas rojas con col y zanahoria
recipe.description: Un guiso reconfortante de lentejas rojas con trozos de col, zanahoria y cebolla, aromatizado con jengibre. Ideal para una cena ligera y nutritiva.
instructions: Pica la col en tiras de 2‑3 cm.
Corta las zanahorias en rodajas finas y la cebolla en cubos pequeños.
Ralla o pica finamente el jengibre (1 cda).
Calienta 2 cda de aceite vegetal en una olla a fuego medio.

Añade las lentejas rojas, la sal y la pimienta.
Reduce a fuego bajo y cocina 20 minutos, removiendo a mitad de tiempo, hasta que las lentejas estén tiernas y el caldo haya espesado ligeramente.
Prueba y ajusta de sal si es necesario. Sirve caliente.
tips: Si te sobra tiempo, puedes tostar ligeramente el jengibre antes de añadirlo para intensificar su aroma.

recipe.title: Pastel al horno de col y patata
recipe.description: Capas de col y patata finamente laminadas, unidas con una masa ligera de harina de trigo, horneadas hasta obtener un gratinado dorado.
instructions: Precalienta el horno a 190°C.
Lava y pela las patatas, luego córtalas en láminas muy finas (≈3 mm).
Corta la col en tiras finas y la cebolla en rodajas delgadas.
En una sartén a fuego medio, calienta 1 cda de aceite vegetal y saltea la cebolla 3 minutos, hasta que empiece a dorarse.
Añade la col y cocina 5 minutos, removiendo, hasta que se ablande. Reserva.
En un bol, mezcla la harina de trigo con 120 ml de agua y una pizca de sal, batiendo hasta obtener una masa líquida sin grumos.
Unta una fuente para horno con la cucharada restante de aceite.

Coloca una capa de láminas de patata en el fondo, cubre con una capa de la mezcla de harina, luego una capa de col salteada. Repite el proceso hasta agotar los ingredientes, terminando con una capa de patata.
Espolvorea una pizca de pimienta y un toque de sal sobre la capa final.
Hornea 25‑30 minutos, a fuego medio, hasta que la superficie esté dorada y las patatas tiernas al pinchar con un tenedor.
Deja reposar 5 minutos antes de cortar y servir.
tips: Si deseas un toque más crujiente, espolvorea un poco de pan rallado (no en la lista, opcional) antes de hornear.
Puedes acompañar el pastel con una salsa de yogur y limón para mayor frescura.

recipe.title: Bobotie de bœuf haché au curry et pain de mie
recipe.description: Un gratin savoureux inspiré du bobotie sud-africain, alliant bœuf haché, pain de mie imbibé de lait, œufs et curry, parfait pour le déjeuner.
instructions: Préchauffe le four à 180°C.
Émince les 2 oignons.
Dans une poêle, fais revenir les oignons à feu moyen 5 minutes, jusqu’à ce qu’ils soient translucides.
Ajoute le 500 g de bœuf haché, fais dorer 8 minutes en émiettant, jusqu’à ce qu’il perde sa couleur rosée.
Vérifie que la température interne du bœuf atteint 71 °C à cœur (utilise un thermomètre, le jus doit être clair).
Saupoudre 2 c. à café de curry en poudre, 1 pincée de sel et 1 pincée de poivre, mélange 1 minute pour libérer les arômes.
Coupe les 4 tranches de pain de mie en petits cubes et place-les dans un bol.

Dans un autre bol, bats les 2 œufs, ajoute une pincée de sel et poivre, puis verse sur la préparation en mélangeant bien.
Transfère le tout dans un plat à gratin, lisse la surface.

Laisse reposer 5 minutes avant de servir.

recipe.description: Un plat mijoté réconfortant où le bœuf haché s’imprègne de curry, servi sur une polenta crémeuse à la farine de maïs.
instructions: Émince l’oignon.

Ajoute le 400 g de bœuf haché, fais cuire 7 minutes en remuant, jusqu’à ce qu’il soit bien bruni.

Écrase la tige de citronnelle, retire la partie dure et hache finement la partie tendre.

recipe.title: Spicy Cauliflower and Tomato Curry
recipe.description: A quick, one‑pot Indian‑style curry featuring urgent cauliflower, fresh tomatoes and fragrant garam masala, perfect for a light dinner.
instructions: Cut the cauliflower into florets (about 200 g).
Dice the tomatoes and set aside.

Add the garlic and ginger; sauté 1 minute more, until fragrant.
Stir in 2 tsp garam masala and cook 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add the cauliflower florets; stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in 1 cup water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer on low heat.
Cover and cook 12 minutes, until cauliflower is tender but not mushy.
Add the diced tomatoes and salt; cook uncovered 5 minutes, until the tomatoes soften and the sauce thickens.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve hot.
tips: If you like extra heat, add a pinch of red chili flakes with the garam masala.
Serve with basmati rice or flatbread for a more filling meal.

recipe.title: Chickpea and Potato Biryani (One‑Pot)
recipe.description: A fragrant, layered biryani using dried chickpeas (pre‑soaked and pre‑cooked), potatoes and aromatic garam masala, cooked entirely in one pot for speed and minimal waste.
instructions: Soak the dried chickpeas in water for at least 4 hours (or overnight).
Drain and rinse the chickpeas; set aside.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1‑cm cubes (about 300 g).

Place the potato cubes in a saucepan, cover with water, bring to a boil over medium‑high heat, and cook 8 minutes, until the pieces are tender when pierced with a knife but still hold their shape. Drain and set aside.

In a separate pot, add the soaked chickpeas, cover with fresh water, bring to a boil, then simmer on low heat for 30 minutes, until the chickpeas are just tender (they should still have a slight bite). Drain and set aside.
Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear; drain.
Dice the tomatoes, finely chop the onion, mince the garlic, and grate the ginger.
Heat 3 tbsp vegetable oil in a large, heavy‑bottomed pot over medium heat; add the onion and sauté 5 minutes, until golden and fragrant.
Add the garlic and ginger; sauté 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in 1.5 tsp garam masala and cook 30 seconds, until aromatic.
Add the pre‑cooked chickpeas and pre‑boiled potatoes; stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in 5 cups water, bring to a rolling boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer; cover and cook 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
Add the rinsed rice, diced tomatoes and the pinch of salt; gently stir to distribute without breaking the rice grains.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 12 minutes, until the rice is fluffy and all liquid is absorbed.
Turn off the heat; let the pot sit, covered, for 5 minutes so the steam finishes cooking the rice.
Fluff the biryani with a fork, garnish with fresh mint leaves, and serve hot.
tips: For extra fragrance, add a few whole cloves and a cinnamon stick with the water; remove before serving.
If you forgot to soak the chickpeas, you can use canned chickpeas (drained and rinsed) and skip the pre‑cooking step, reducing the total cook time by about 10 minutes.

recipe.title: Cauliflower, Potato & Tomato Pilaf with Garam Masala
recipe.description: A fragrant one‑pot vegan pilaf that highlights urgent cauliflower, tender potatoes, and juicy tomatoes, seasoned with warm garam masala and aromatic spices.
instructions: Cut the cauliflower into small florets and rinse; peel the potatoes and dice them into 1‑cm cubes.
Blanch the cauliflower florets in boiling water for 3 minutes, until just tender but still bright, then drain and set aside.
Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear; soak for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced potatoes and sauté 5 minutes, stirring, until the edges turn golden.
Add the drained cauliflower to the pot and stir‑fry 2 minutes more.
Stir in 1 tsp ground cumin, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 2 tsp garam masala; cook 1 minute, until the spices become fragrant.
Chop the tomatoes roughly and add them to the pot; cook 4 minutes, stirring, until they soften and release juices.
Add the soaked basmati rice, 400 ml water, 1 pinch salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Bring to a boil over medium‑high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Turn off the heat and let the pilaf sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork.
Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro before serving.
tips: If you have a pressure cooker, you can cook the rice and vegetables together in 8 minutes, saving time.
For extra crunch, reserve a few cauliflower florets, toss them with a little oil and bake at 200 °C for 10 minutes, then stir into the finished pilaf.
Adjust the amount of garam masala to taste; a milder version uses 1 tsp.

recipe.title: Quesadilla de tortilla con queso fresco y salsa de tomate y serrano
recipe.description: Una quesadilla crujiente rellena de queso fresco fundido y acompañada de una fresca salsa picante de tomate y chile serrano.
instructions: Pica finamente los 2 tomates y el chile serrano.
Calienta 1 cda de aceite vegetal en un sartén a fuego medio y sofríe el tomate y el chile durante 4 minutos, hasta que el tomate se deshaga y la salsa espese ligeramente; sazona con 1 pizca de sal.
Ralla o desmenuza el queso fresco (120 g).
Coloca una tortilla en otro sartén limpio a fuego medio, distribuye 30 g de queso fresco sobre la mitad y dobla la tortilla.
Cocina la quesadilla 2 minutos por lado, hasta que esté dorada y el queso se haya fundido.
Repite con las tortillas restantes y el resto del queso.
Sirve las quesadillas calientes acompañadas de la salsa de tomate y serrano.
tips: Si te gusta más picante, añade el chile entero al sofrito y retira las semillas antes de picar.
Puedes añadir un poco de cilantro picado a la salsa para mayor frescura.

recipe.title: Huevos rancheros con frijoles negros y tortilla
recipe.description: Clásico desayuno mexicano: huevos estrellados sobre una cama de frijoles negros, bañados en salsa de tomate y chile, servido con tortilla caliente.
instructions: Abre la lata de frijoles negros, escúrrelos y enjuágalos bajo agua fría.
Calienta 1 cda de aceite vegetal en una cacerola a fuego medio, añade los frijoles y cocina 5 minutos, removiendo, hasta que estén tibios.

Calienta las 2 tortillas en un comal o sartén 30 segundos por lado.
Para servir, coloca una tortilla en cada plato, cubre con la mitad de los frijoles, coloca dos huevos estrellados encima, y vierte la salsa de tomate y serrano por encima.
tips: Si prefieres los frijoles más cremosos, aplástalos ligeramente con una cuchara antes de servir.
Añade unas hojas de cilantro fresco picado para dar color y aroma.

recipe.title: Sopa ligera de frijoles negros, tomate y huevo pochado
recipe.description: Una sopa reconfortante y rápida, con frijoles negros, tomate y un huevo pochado que aporta proteína y cremosidad.
instructions: Abre la lata de frijoles negros, escúrrelos y enjuágalos.
Pica los 2 tomates y el chile serrano.
En una olla mediana, calienta 1 cda de aceite vegetal a fuego medio y sofríe el tomate y el chile 4 minutos, hasta que el tomate se deshaga.
Añade los frijoles negros escurridos y 500 ml de agua a la olla; lleva a ebullición y cocina 8 minutos, removiendo ocasionalmente, hasta que la sopa tenga cuerpo.

Sazona la sopa con 1 pizca de sal y ajusta el picante al gusto.
Calienta las 2 tortillas en un comal 30 segundos por lado y córtalas en tiras para servir como acompañamiento.
Sirve la sopa en tazones, coloca un huevo pochado sobre cada porción y acompaña con tiras de tortilla crujiente.
tips: Si la sopa queda muy espesa, agrega un poco más de agua caliente.
Puedes añadir un chorrito de jugo de limón al final para realzar el sabor.

recipe.description: Un ragoût créole épicé où la morue salée se marie aux ignames fondantes, relevé de piment antillais et parfumé aux zestes de citron vert.
instructions: Rince la morue salée sous l’eau froide puis fais-la tremper dans 800 ml d’eau froide pendant 30 minutes, en changeant l’eau une fois, pour désaler.

Émince finement 2 tiges de cives (partie verte) et réserve le reste pour la garniture.

Retire le piment, ajoute les cives émincées, le jus du citron vert, sale et poivre à ton goût. Mélange 1 minute.

recipe.title: Plantains rôtis au four, crumble de farine et vinaigrette citron‑cive
recipe.description: Plantains mûrs rôtis jusqu’à caramel, recouverts d’un crumble léger à la farine, le tout nappé d’une vinaigrette citron‑cive fraîche.
instructions: Préchauffe le four à 200 °C.
Épluche les plantains, coupe‑les en rondelles d’environ 1 cm d’épaisseur.
Dispose les rondelles sur une plaque recouverte de papier cuisson, badigeonne chaque côté avec 1 c. à soupe d’huile végétale.
Enfourne 12 minutes, tourne les rondelles, puis poursuis 8 minutes jusqu’à ce qu’elles soient dorées et légèrement caramélisées.

Pendant ce temps, prépare le crumble : mélange 60 g de farine avec 1 pincée de sel et 1 pincée de poivre, ajoute 2 c. à soupe d’huile végétale et travaille du bout des doigts jusqu’à obtenir une texture sableuse.
Répartis le crumble uniformément sur les plantains encore chauds, remets au four 5 minutes pour dorer le dessus.
Pour la vinaigrette, hache finement 4 tiges de cives (partie blanche et verte). Dans un bol, mélange le jus des 2 citrons verts, 1 c. à soupe d’huile végétale, les cives hachées, sel et poivre.
Verse la vinaigrette sur les plantains avant de servir.
tips: Choisis des plantains très mûrs (peau noire) pour obtenir un caramel naturel.
Le crumble peut être aromatisé avec une pincée de paprika ou de curry si disponible.

recipe.title: Peruvian‑style Chicken and Corn Stew
recipe.description: A hearty, one‑pot stew that blends tender chicken breast with sweet corn, potatoes, and a bright yellow chili paste, finished with a squeeze of lime for freshness.
instructions: Dice the red onion (1 piece) and set aside.
Cut the potatoes (4 pieces) into 2‑cm cubes.
Slice the corn kernels off the cobs (3 pieces) using a sharp knife.
Season the chicken breasts (2 pieces) with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch pepper.
In a large pot, heat a splash of oil over medium heat; add the onion and sauté 3 minutes, until translucent.
Add the chicken breasts, browning 4 minutes per side, until the outside is golden and the internal temperature reaches 74 °C (check with a thermometer).
Remove the chicken temporarily, add the potatoes and corn kernels, stir for 2 minutes.
Stir in the yellow chili paste (2 tbsp) and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.
Return the chicken to the pot, add water (800 ml) and bring to a gentle boil over medium heat.
Reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 20 minutes, until potatoes are fork‑tender and chicken is cooked through.
While the stew simmers, rinse the rice (200 g) and place in a saucepan with 400 ml water, a pinch of salt; bring to boil, then reduce to low heat, cover and cook 12 minutes, until water is absorbed.
Turn off the heat, let the rice sit covered 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Finish the stew by stirring in lime juice (2 tbsp) and adjusting seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Serve the stew over a bed of rice, garnished with an extra lime wedge if desired.
tips: If you prefer a thicker broth, mash a few potato pieces before adding the rice.
Use the corn cob shells to make a quick stock for extra flavor.

recipe.title: Baked Lime‑Chili Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Corn Salad
recipe.description: Oven‑roasted chicken breasts glazed with lime and yellow chili paste, served alongside crisp roasted potatoes and a bright corn‑on‑the‑cob salad.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Wash the potatoes (4 pieces) and cut them into 2‑cm wedges.
Place the potato wedges on a baking sheet, drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil, season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch pepper, and toss to coat.
Roast the potatoes on the middle rack for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
While potatoes roast, trim the ends off the chicken breasts (2 pieces) and pat dry.
In a small bowl, mix yellow chili paste (1 tbsp) with lime juice (3 tbsp) and the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.
Brush the chicken breasts generously with the chili‑lime mixture, then season with a pinch of salt.

When the potatoes have 10 minutes left, place the chicken on a second baking sheet and bake alongside the potatoes for 10 minutes, then flip and bake another 8 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 74 °C and the juices run clear.
Meanwhile, bring a pot of water to boil, add the corn cobs (2 pieces) and cook 5 minutes, until tender. Drain and let cool slightly.
Thinly slice the red onion (1 piece). In a bowl, combine the corn kernels (cut from the cobs), sliced onion, a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and the juice of any remaining lime.
Remove chicken and potatoes from the oven; let the chicken rest 3 minutes before slicing.
Plate sliced chicken atop the roasted potatoes, with the corn salad on the side.
tips: For extra char, finish the chicken under the broiler for 2 minutes after the bake.
If you like a little sweetness, add a teaspoon of honey to the chili‑lime glaze.

recipe.title: Cold Corn‑Potato Chicken Salad with Lime Vinaigrette
recipe.description: A refreshing, light salad perfect for dinner, combining shredded chicken, diced potatoes, sweet corn, red onion, and a tangy lime‑yellow chili vinaigrette.
instructions: Place the potatoes (4 pieces) in a pot, cover with cold water, add a pinch of salt, and bring to a boil over medium heat.
When water boils, reduce to a gentle simmer and cook 12 minutes, until potatoes are fork‑tender.
While potatoes cook, bring another pot of water to boil, add the corn cob (1 piece) and cook 5 minutes.
Remove the corn, let cool, then cut the kernels off the cob.
Season the chicken breasts (2 pieces) with a pinch of salt and pepper.
In a skillet over medium heat, add a splash of oil and sear the chicken 6 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 74 °C.

Drain the potatoes, rinse under cold water to stop cooking, and cut into 1‑cm dice.
Finely dice the red onion (1 piece).
